title: NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own): Taking Back an Elevation Certificate Re-Rate Credit on Cancellation
content:
Where a policy under the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) received a risk premium re-rate credit from an applied Elevation Certificate, a cancellation takes back the part of that credit that falls after the cancellation effective date.

**Rule.** The re-rate credit a cancellation takes back is settled as follows: when the Elevation Certificate behind the policy's latest risk premium re-rate credit took effect on or before the cancellation effective date within the term the cancellation takes effect in, it is that re-rate credit for the days from the cancellation effective date to the end of that term over the days from the certificate's effective date to the end of that term; when the certificate took effect after the cancellation effective date, it is the whole re-rate credit; otherwise nothing is taken back.

## Records read

The policy's latest risk premium re-rate credit on the premium account, the term it belongs to, and the effective date of the Elevation Certificate behind it in the servicing file.

## Ladder

| Elevation Certificate effective date | Taken back |
|---|---|
| on or before the cancellation effective date, in the term the cancellation takes effect in | the re-rate credit times the days from the cancellation effective date to the end of that term, over the days from the certificate's effective date to the end of that term |
| after the cancellation effective date | the whole re-rate credit |
| in an earlier term, or no re-rate credit | nothing |

## Cases (hypothetical)

- Re-rate credit 300.00; certificate effective with 150 days of the term left; cancellation effective with 60 days left: 300.00 times 60 over 150 is 120.00 taken back.
- Certificate effective after the cancellation effective date: 300.00 taken back.
